children: Stock index futures were higher on Thursday, a day after Wall Street ended lower following the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike.
Here are the five news items investors should watch:
Fed raises rates as Trump calls for 1%:
The Federal Reserve, led by Kevin Warsh, raised interest rates by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, its first

in more than three years. President Donald Trump said the U.S. should have the world’s lowest rates at 1% or less, while Warsh said the increase was needed to restrict economic growth enough to bring down inflation.
Huawei accelerates AI chip roadmap:
Huawei Technologies plans to launch two new AI chips in 2027 as it expands its AI computing business and challenges Nvidia
. Rotating chairman David Wang said the 960DT is
for Q1, followed by the Ascend 960PR in Q3, accelerating the previously disclosed roadmap for the Ascend 960.
Japan, U.S. discuss semiconductor factory:
Japan and the U.S. are discussing a semiconductor factory estimated to cost ¥2T-¥3T ($12.9B-$19.3B), Nikkei reported. The facility would be operated by GlobalFoundries
as part of Japan’s $550B U.S. investment agreement, with the countries also discussing a
data center involving SoftBank Group
OpenAI flags unexpected model behavior:
OpenAI

disclosed examples of AI models displaying unexpected or concerning behavior under a new framework for reporting system misalignment. The incidents included attempts to bypass restrictions, conceal mistakes, and fabricate information, while the company said the industry has not sufficiently solved alignment and monitoring challenges.
Anthropic calls for external AI oversight:
Sarah Heck, Anthropic's

public policy head, said AI companies cannot be expected to manage their oversight. Speaking at the Politico Decoded Summit, she called for government involvement in regulating increasingly capable AI systems and said companies and policymakers need to determine an appropriate approach.
